- [For Godot Developers](https://developers.brickverse.gg/moving-to-brickverse/for-godot-developers): BrickVerse uses Godot technology internally, but BrickVerse games do not directly use the full Godot Engine API. Creators build against the BrickVerse Game API and write gameplay scripts in BrickLua, a fork of Luau.
- [Auto-translating your Roblox Luau to BrickLua](https://developers.brickverse.gg/moving-to-brickverse/for-roblox-developers/auto-translating-your-roblox-luau-to-bricklua): `RBLXLuau2BrickLua` helps migrate Roblox Luau scripts to BrickLua, the scripting language used by BrickVerse.

- [For Roblox Developers](https://developers.brickverse.gg/moving-to-brickverse/for-roblox-developers): BrickVerse will feel familiar to Roblox developers because both platforms use an instance hierarchy, service-based APIs, Luau-style scripting, and a multiplayer client-server runtime.
- [For Unity Developers](https://developers.brickverse.gg/moving-to-brickverse/for-unity-developers): BrickVerse is not a general-purpose engine project that you compile and ship yourself. It is a hosted multiplayer game platform with an instance hierarchy, built-in services, integrated publishing, and sandboxed scripting through BrickLua.
- [For Unreal Engine Developers](https://developers.brickverse.gg/moving-to-brickverse/for-unreal-engine-developers): BrickVerse provides a hosted, authoritative multiplayer runtime with a service-based Game API and scripting through BrickLua, a fork of Luau.
- [For Web Developers](https://developers.brickverse.gg/moving-to-brickverse/for-web-developers): BrickVerse scripting is approachable for JavaScript and TypeScript developers because BrickLua is dynamic, event-driven, module-friendly, and commonly uses asynchronous service APIs.
- [Overview](https://developers.brickverse.gg/moving-to-brickverse/overview): BrickVerse is a multiplayer game platform with an instance-based Game API and a scripting language based on a fork of Luau.
- [Upload Limits and Restrictions](https://developers.brickverse.gg/moving-to-brickverse/upload-limits-and-restrictions): BrickVerse applies creation and upload limits to **Universes, Worlds, Entitlements, and Developer Assets**. These limits help keep the platform reliable, provide reasonable resource availability for creators, and reduce automated or abusive

- [Welcome](https://developers.brickverse.gg/): This is the official developer hub for creating games and interactive experiences on the BrickVerse platform. Whether you're building your first world or scaling a large multiplayer experience, these docs give you the tools and knowledge to
- [Building a UI](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/building-a-ui): BrickVerse interfaces use Instances. The local player's UI hierarchy is available through the global `PlayerGUI`.
- [Client vs Server](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/client-vs-server): BrickVerse multiplayer games run across an authoritative server and individual player clients.
- [Common Scripting Patterns](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/common-scripting-patterns): These patterns help keep BrickLua systems reliable, secure, and maintainable.
- [Creating NPCs](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/creating-npcs): An `NPC` is a physical character controller with health, movement, navigation, appearance, tools, and character state.
- [Creating Parts](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/creating-parts): `Part` is a basic physical building object. It inherits hierarchy, transform, physics, and appearance behavior.
- [Events](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/events): Events allow scripts to react when something happens. They are preferable to repeatedly checking state in a loop.
- [Functions](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/functions): Functions group reusable behavior. They can accept arguments, return values, call other functions, and be passed to events as callbacks.
- [HTTP Requests](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/http-requests): The global `Http` service sends supported web requests from BrickLua.
- [Inventory Systems](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/inventory-systems): An inventory system tracks which items a player owns and how many of each item they have.
- [Leaderboards](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/leaderboards): BrickVerse leaderboard statistics use `Stat` Instances and the global `Stats` service.
- [Making a Tool](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/making-a-tool): A `Tool` is an item that an NPC or Player can hold, equip, activate, deactivate, and drop.
- [Modules](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/modules): A `ModuleScript` contains reusable BrickLua code. Modules reduce duplication and make larger games easier to organize.
- [NetworkService](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/networkservice): BrickVerse client-server communication uses `NetworkEvent` Instances and typed `NetMessage` payloads.
- [BrickLua Tutorials](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau): BrickLua is BrickVerse's scripting language. It is based on a fork of Luau and runs inside the BrickVerse sandbox.
- [Saving Data](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/saving-data): Use the global `Datastore` service to save data between sessions. Datastores are available only from server scripts.
- [Tables](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/tables): Tables are BrickLua's main data structure. They can represent arrays, dictionaries, sets, records, configuration, and object-like modules.
- [Universe Configs](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/universe-configs): Universe Configs provide live configuration values for a Universe. They are useful for values that may need to change without publishing a new build.
- [Using JSON](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/using-json): JSON is a text format for structured data. BrickLua's built-in `json` object converts between JSON strings and BrickLua values.
- [Using Tags](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/using-tags): Tags attach searchable labels to Instances. They are useful when objects share a role but are stored in different parts of the hierarchy.
- [Variables and Types](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/variables-and-types): Variables store values that your script can reuse and change. BrickLua supports Luau's gradual type system, so you can write scripts with or without explicit type annotations.
- [Working with Players](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/working-with-players): The global `Players` service manages connected players.
- [Your First Script](https://developers.brickverse.gg/scripting-with-luau/your-first-script): A script is a piece of BrickLua code that runs inside a World. BrickVerse provides three script types:
